howToCalculate.title: How to estimate PJ take-home cash
howToCalculate.p1: The estimate starts from monthly PJ revenue, calculates Simples Nacional DAS, then subtracts INSS, IRRF, accounting, costs, and entered withholdings.
howToCalculate.p2: The result shows available cash flow, not a payslip, bookkeeping profit, or official profit distribution.

simples.title: What enters Brazilian Simples Nacional for PJ
simples.p1: For Annex III and Annex V, the calculator selects the bracket by RBT12 and applies the effective-rate formula in effect since 2018.
simples.p2: Activities, retained ISS, revenue segregation, sublimits, and official PGDAS-D choices can change the final amount.

fatorR.title: How factor R changes Annex III and Annex V
fatorR.p1: Factor R is FS12 divided by RBT12. For services subject to factor R, 28% or more points to Annex III.
fatorR.p2: FS12 can include pro-labore, remuneration, and charges from the prior 12 months, so review the field carefully.

proLabore.title: Pro-labore, INSS, and IRRF for PJ
proLabore.p1: The entered pro-labore is used to estimate social-security contribution and 2026 monthly IRRF.
proLabore.p2: INSS modes are assumptions: 20%, 11%, MEI reference, manual, or no deduction.

limitations.title: Why MEI, Lucro Presumido, and official accounting can change the result
limitations.p1: MEI, Annex IV, Lucro Presumido, Lucro Real, municipal ISS, and withholdings have their own rules and are not closed in this version.
limitations.p2: Profit distribution depends on bookkeeping, contract, regime, and professional review.

contract.title: What to compare before accepting a PJ contract
contract.text: Besides monthly cash, consider unpaid vacation, no 13th salary, severance, benefits, late payment, adjustments, emergency reserve, and contract risk.

disclaimer.title: Important notice
disclaimer.text: This tool is an educational estimate, not legal, tax, accounting, social-security, labor, contract, or investment advice. Accountant, PGDAS-D, eSocial/DCTFWeb, municipality, bookkeeping, official documents, and professional review prevail.

q1.question: What is PJ salary?
q1.answer: It is an informal way to describe what remains for the owner after company revenue, taxes, pro-labore, contributions, and costs. It is not CLT salary.

q2.question: Does this work for MEI?
q2.answer: Not as a full calculation. It can show a 5% MEI social-security reference, but it does not calculate full DAS-MEI.

q3.question: Which Simples annex does it use?
q3.answer: It uses Annex III, Annex V, automatic factor R, or a manual effective rate entered by the user.

q4.question: What is factor R?
q4.answer: It is FS12/RBT12. For services subject to factor R, 28% or more points to Annex III; below 28% points to Annex V.

q5.question: Is pro-labore mandatory?
q5.answer: The calculator does not determine legal obligation. It uses entered pro-labore as an assumption for INSS, IRRF, and FS12.

q6.question: Are PJ INSS and IRRF the same as CLT?
q6.answer: No. Here they are pro-labore/individual assumptions, different from a CLT payslip.

q7.question: Is the net amount distributable profit?
q7.answer: No. Available cash is estimated cash flow and does not validate bookkeeping or profit distribution.

q8.question: Why can my accountant or PGDAS-D differ?
q8.answer: Activity, municipality, withholdings, annexes, sublimits, revenue history, payroll, and bookkeeping can change the official calculation.

q9.question: Does it compare CLT vs PJ?
q9.answer: No. This page estimates monthly PJ cash flow; full contract comparison belongs in another tool.
